task.title: Break tables across pages
task.shortdesc: A long table continues on the next pages. You can repeat its header and its footer on every page, keep rows whole, and force a page break between rows.

info.p: A table breaks between its rows. When a row does not fit in the space that is left on the page, CSSMedia decides by its height:

ul.li: A row that is less than half as high as the page goes whole to the next page.
A taller row breaks inside. Each cell of the row continues on the next page where it stopped, and the cells that have ended stay empty.

info.p: To keep a row whole in any case, give the rows break-inside: avoid. A row that is taller than a page cannot be kept whole, and it breaks anyway.

step.cmd: Repeat the header and the footer

info.p: The rows of a header group or a footer group are repeated on every page that the table uses, when the group has break-inside: avoid. A group that is taller than a quarter of the page is not repeated, so that the pages keep room for the rows of the body:
The footer repeats at the end of each page, directly after the last row of the page. Without break-inside: avoid, the header is only at the top of the table, and the footer is only at its end.

image.alt: Two pages. The first has a header row, four rows and the first lines of a fifth row that does not fit. The second page has the header row again, the last lines of the fifth row and two more rows.

info.p: The properties break-before and break-after work on rows and on row groups. With the value page the table continues on a new page, and with avoid CSSMedia tries not to break there:

A table is not held back by orphans and widows: a single row can be alone on a page. If you do not want that, use break-before: avoid and break-after: avoid on the rows that must stay together. The break moves to an earlier place between rows.
